title: Early diagnosis of light chain amyloidosis
text:
Light chain amyloidosis is an understudied and underserved blood disorder associated with delayed and under
diagnosis, particularly among Black individuals, despite warning signs in the form of a premalignant MGUS state
and multiple preexisting precursor diagnoses that frequently occur. This project will study patterns of precursor
diagnoses in AL amyloidosis cases, associated racial differences, and identification of potentially undiagnosed
AL amyloidosis patients using Bayesian machine learning algorithms. This application, in response to the NOSI:
Diagnostics and Disease Management Tools for Use in Underserved Populations (NOT-HL-22-006), will create
pathways to early diagnosis of AL amyloidosis when it is more treatable, yielding improved outcomes and
prolonged survival.

title: Regulation of Renal Tubular Mg2+ Handling by MUC1 and Lactation
text:
Magnesium is an essential mineral that is critical for bone density, but very little is known about how the body
regulates magnesium absorption and excretion. Lactation represents a stressful physiologic period during which
female mammals must provide large quantities of bone minerals, including magnesium, to offspring in the form
of breastmilk. This project explores the physiologic changes that occur in the kidney in lactation to provide a
better understanding of how the body regulates levels of magnesium and other essential minerals.

title: Reducing Intratumoral Bacteria to Enhance Anti-Tumor Immunity in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
text:
The proposed project will determine the mechanisms by which intratumoral bacteria modulate the
immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment and impact treatment response in head and neck can-
cer. In this co-clinical trial, we will: 1) Utilize novel oral cancer co-infection preclinical murine models to under-
stand immunologic factors driving bacteria-induced tumor growth and immunotherapy resistance; and, 2) Con-
duct a window-of-opportunity clinical trial for oral cancer patients to evaluate the efficacy of antibiotic treatment
in reshaping intratumoral immunity. Our studies will improve the understanding of the cellular and molecular
processes underlying bacteria-driven tumor immunosuppression, and explore ways to reverse these effects,
providing a foundation to guide future therapeutic development.

title: Multi-electroplasmonic nanoantenna arrays for wireless transmembrane-level recording of cardiomyocyte action potentials with sub-micrometer resolution
text:
Electrophysiology is essential in developing novel therapeutics against cardiovascular diseases, the leading cause of death
worldwide. This proposal introduces a novel nanophotonic device to wirelessly perform electrophysiological studies of
cardiac models in vitro with unprecedented resolution and long-term stability. This technological development is projected
to impact fundamental and translational cardiac research significantly and, in the long term, contribute to relieving the social
and economic burden of cardiovascular disorders on society.

title: Novel Radiomics for Predicting Response to Immunotherapy for Lung Cancer
text:
RELEVANCE: Only 1 in 5 lung cancer patients treated with immunotherapy (IO) has a favorable response.
Additionally, the cost of IO is extremely high, >$200K/year per patient. The goal of this project is to develop novel
computational radiomic tools which in conjunction with routine CT scans from IO clinical trials will allow for (1)
identifying pre-IO therapy as to which non-small cell lung cancer patients could potentially benefit from immune
checkpoint inhibitors and (2) quantitatively monitor serial changes in tumor heterogeneity during IO treatment for
early identification of responders and non-responders.

title: Zoonotic Uropathogenic Escherichia coli in Northwest Ecuador: Incidence and Risk Factors
text: Urinary tract infections affect millions of Americans each year and are most commonly caused by uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC). This project will identify animal reservoirs and transmission pathways that contribute to human UPEC infections by studying a unique high-exposure setting where zoonotic transmission can be more readily detected and characterized. The findings will improve the ability to trace the sources of UPEC infections, strengthen surveillance for antimicrobial-resistant strains, and inform prevention strategies aimed at reducing the burden of UTIs in the United States.

title: Biogenic Gas Nanostructures as Molecular Imaging Reporters for Ultrasound
text:
Ultrasound is among the world’s most widely used biomedical imaging technologies, but plays a relatively small
role in molecular and cellular imaging due to a lack of contrast agents connected to specific aspects of cellular
function such as gene expression and intracellular signaling. To address this limitation, we are developing
acoustic biomolecules – proteins that can be imaged with ultrasound and serve as targeted nanoscale contrast
agents and genetically encoded acoustic reporter genes. In this project, we will advance the engineering of these
unique proteins and related ultrasound methods and apply them to imaging tumors and tumor-infiltrating immune
cells.

title: Elucidating alternative polyadenylation regulation during prostate cancer progression to castration-resistance
text:
This project aims to illuminate the role of alternative polyadenylation (APA) as a key post-transcriptional
regulatory mechanism propelling prostate cancer towards its lethal stages. By delving into APA, we will enrich
the existing comprehension of the transcriptional processes fueling prostate cancer progression. The
prospective clinical implications of this research could revolutionize our approach, providing a foundation for
novel APA-focused therapeutic strategies for prostate cancer.

title: Therapeutic Manufacturing Shared Resource
text: THERAPEUTIC MANUFACTURING SHARED RESOURCE The Therapeutic Manufacturing Shared Resource (TMSR) of the Fred Hutchinson/University of Washington/Seattle Children’s Cancer Consortium is located at Fred Hutch and has two current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) Phase I/II clinical product clean room manufacturing facilities. This resource provides translational services that enable complex cancer research treatments to progress from the lab to the bedside. TMSR provides clinical manufacturing services for a multitude of products for Consortium investigators that span from traditional biologics to advanced cell and gene therapy applications. The FACT- (Foundation for the Accreditation of Cellular Therapy) accredited Cell Processing Facility (CPF) can produce human hematopoietic or immune-competent cells for advanced cell and gene therapy products, specializing in TCR and CAR-T manufacturing processes. The Biologics Processing Facility (BPF) manufactured various products, such as cellular products from microbial and mammalian culture systems, including monoclonal antibodies, fusion proteins, conjugates, plasmids, peptide vaccines and viral vectors. These production services provided by TMSR follow cGMP and include operations staff that are highly trained in clinical manufacturing. All processing facilities and equipment are maintained in a qualified cGMP state and all products are subject to Quality Control testing and Quality Assurance systems that ensure FDA compliance for the safe manufacture and release of clinical trial materials. The TMSR also provides Process Development, Process Engineering and Materials Control resources to maintain high manufacturing success rates and fully facilitate the translation of projects from faculty labs into the cGMP manufacturing facility in a cost-effective, compliant, and timely manner for complex therapy modalities. Through Product Management facilitation, the TMSR works closely with investigators within a series of team structures to ensure informed and appropriate planning, manufacturing process development, production readiness and process performance analysis and improvement. Utilizing the TMSR, Consortium members have initiated a range of Phase I and II clinical trials that have advanced the scientific understanding of cancer therapies. The TMSR maintains a strong culture of continuous process improvement. We continue to develop and refine our capabilities through monitoring and analyzing performance metrics. This also enables the development of strategic planning to keep pace with future needs. Additionally, the more recent expansion of our capabilities and services in Process Development and Process Engineering provides for more efficient examination and on-boarding of new manufacturing technologies and equipment.

title: Development of Spectral Phase Contrast Micro-CT
text:
The objective of this proposal is to develop a next-generation micro-CT system that offers low-dose, fast x-ray
phase-contrast imaging (PCI) for soft tissue imaging. Our proposed system will use cutting-edge high
resolution spectral detectors, allowing direct comparison of PCI micro-CT with attenuation-based spectral
micro-CT. PCI may provide significant reductions in dose coupled with enhanced contrast and higher fine-
structure visibility as advantages for cancer research in animal models.

title: Deriving Real World Insights to Inform Trials for Pregnant Individuals Using Electronic Health Records and Machine Learning
text: Pregnant women are often excluded from clinical trials, leaving patients, clinicians, and policymakers with limited evidence to guide safe and effective care during pregnancy. This project will use real-world data, artificial intelligence, and privacy-preserving methods to improve how pregnancy-related populations and outcomes are identified and how trial eligibility criteria are designed. The results may help make future pregnancy studies safer, more inclusive, and more relevant to real-world patients, ultimately improving evidence-based care for pregnant women and their infants.

title: Peripheral vestibular hypofunction and neurosensory coding
text:
The investigation to be conducted through the present research strategy aims to establish the
histopathologic and pathophysiologic correlates of vestibular hypofunction induced by the common ototoxin,
gentamicin. The primary objective is to determine the physiologic signatures of the functional decrements
providing insight into strategies through which these conditions can be identified in suspected patients. The
histopathologic correlates will identify the cellular components of the inner ear vestibular epithelia that are
associated with these deficits and, therefore, potential targets of protective and rehabilitative strategies.

title: CORE C Technology Implementation/Development and Correlative Sciences
text:
CORE C PROJECT NARRATIVE 
Core C will support the goals of the three proposed projects in three ways; 1. Developing improved methods to 
manufacture gene-edited CAR T and HSPC products and transferring these processes to the manufacturing 
Core B to ultimately translate research bench concepts to bedside therapies; 2. Supporting the three proposed 
clinical trials by performing specialized assays on product and patient samples to describe product 
characteristics and safety aspects and to identify the fate of infused CAR T or CD34+ cells to predict and evaluate 
their impact on disease; 3. Refining and developing new sophisticated analysis platforms for characterizing 
products and clinical trial samples on a molecular and clonal level.

title: Credentialing next-generation human glioma models for precision therapeutics
text:
Gliomas, the most common primary brain tumor in humans, are genetically heterogeneous tumors. Our
goal is to credential novel genetically engineered human models of gliomas against patient-derived models
using comprehensive biological, molecular, drug therapy profiling. Models will be designed to genetically
match their human counterparts and used to develop rational combination therapies that combat drug
resistance mechanisms.

title: Multiplex gene sequencing and metabolomics analysis from newborn dried blood spots to improve screening and diagnosis of metabolic disorders.
text: Newborn screening saves lives by identifying infants with serious inherited disorders before symptoms occur, but false-positive results can delay diagnosis and create unnecessary follow-up. This project will evaluate genomic and metabolomic markers that can improve interpretation of abnormal newborn screening results and support development of more accurate second-tier testing.

title: The INSPIRE trial -Integrating Serial and Parallel Interconnected Respiratory Elements for sparing post-radiotherapy pulmonary function
text:
In current clinical practice, when we treat cancerous lesions in the lung with radiation, we regard the
lung as a uniform, homogeneous organ. However, damage to airway segments (ignored in current
clinical practice) causes downstream "functioning" lung volumes to lose their supply line and
therefore renders them incapable of exchanging oxygen with the blood. In this proposed clinical trial,
we will compare the post-radiotherapy function in patients who receive our recently-developed
airway-sparing radiotherapy technique with the function of patients who receive the current
standard-of care radiotherapy, and show that, by preserving airways and connected functional lung
regions, patients will be able to retain a larger amount of their lung function, which will have a direct,
positive impact on their post-treatment quality of life.

title: Dissecting the role of tumor suppressing microRNAs in angiosarcoma
text:
Angiosarcomas are aggressive and metastatic vascular sarcomas of endothelial cells with a very poor
prognosis. Mouse models indicate miRNAs function as critical tumor suppressors in angiosarcoma. This
proposal aims to identify these miRNAs, understand their mechanistic regulatory network, and target this
unique vulnerability therapeutically with a repurposed antibiotic that enhances miRNA biogenesis.

title: Prediction of Risk and Resilience in Psychosis and Bipolar Spectrum Disorders: A Translational Multimodal Study
text:
Psychosis and bipolar spectrum disorders (PBSD) rank among the most globally disabling conditions, leading to
poor functional outcomes, diminished quality of life, and premature mortality, yet current risk prediction methods
remain limited to specialized research settings. This innovative project will first identify multimodal predictors of
risk and resilience from landmark clinical high-risk studies, then translate these findings to the population level
by developing and validating longitudinal machine learning models within electronic health records. Through the
development prediction tools that enable personalized screening, this research will not only improve early
identification and intervention for PBSD at the population level but also address health disparities and enhance
clinical decision-making, directly advancing NIMH's strategic goals for accessible, scalable mental health
screening and treatment.

title: Personalized Response through Integrated Measurement for Depression in Primary care (PRIME-DEP-PC) for Older Adults with Multimorbidity
text:
Depression is common in older adults with multimorbidity, who are overwhelmingly treated for depression by their
primary care providers with limited effectiveness. This project seeks to develop and pilot the “Personalized Response
through Integrated Measurement of Depression in PC” (PRIME-DEP-PC), a new tool to improve how depression is
managed in primary care for older adults with multimorbidity. The proposed study will establish the feasibility and
acceptability of PRIME-DEP-PC, with the ultimate goal of improving the mental health outcomes of this growing
population.

title: Mechanisms of PCDH19-clustering epilepsy
text:
PCDH19-clustering epilepsy (PCE) is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy predominantly
affecting girls and caused by pathogenic variants in an X-linked gene. Using a mouse model that we recently
developed, we propose to study how this unique inheritance pattern leads to abnormal interneuron
development and susceptibility to seizures. This work will provide insight into disease mechanisms and may
identify a therapeutic target to treat patients with PCE.
